title: Billions in losses, no dividends: Inside the AI IPO frenzy
source_used: The Sydney Morning Herald (column by Victoria Devine)
key_facts: A personal-finance column explaining what retail investors should know before the Anthropic and OpenAI IPOs
Anthropic filed with the SEC on 1 June after a $65bn round at a $965bn valuation; Bloomberg reports the float is now likely mid-November and Reuters reports it seeks a valuation above $2 trillion
OpenAI's IPO has been pushed to 2027; it is reportedly raising at least $30bn privately at about $1.4tn
Anthropic's prospectus, reported by Reuters, shows a net loss of about $42bn in 2025, of which about $34bn was an accounting charge; operating loss rose from about $3bn to about $8bn
SpaceX listed in June at about $1.8tn, rose above $2tn, later fell about 30 percent from its high and pays no dividend
Whether Australian retail investors can apply for IPO shares is not yet known
quote_evidence: Both OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, and Anthropic, the company behind Claude, are preparing to go public.
The Anthropic prospectus, reported on by Reuters this week, shows the company recorded a net loss of around $US42 billion last year, although the headline figure needs some context.
why_it_matters_hint: Retail investors are being told to read the prospectus: huge losses and no dividends come with the AI IPOs
event_date: Column published 3-4 Oct 2026; underlying filings earlier this week
notes: Opinion/explainer column; facts rest on Reuters and Bloomberg reporting earlier in the week. No new event.
